items.name: full
items.prompt:
You are a senior YouTube Shorts editor and audio producer reverse-engineering this video for a research report. Watch the ENTIRE video WITH SOUND, start to finish. Write in English. Use [mm:ss] timestamps everywhere. Be precise and concrete; if something is not audible or not visible, say so instead of guessing.

Return exactly these sections:

1. FIRST 3 SECONDS: what is on screen in the very first frame and how it moves; the first spoken words verbatim; whether music or a sound effect starts before or with the voice; anything that would stop a viewer scrolling.
2. TIMED EDIT LOG: one line per visual change for the whole video: [mm:ss] what is on screen (satellite map / globe / 3D object / character / photo / text card), what moves and how (zoom, pan, highlight fill, glow, arrows, flags, objects popping in, transitions), on-screen text exactly as shown, sound effects, music changes, and the narration sentence playing at that moment.
3. NARRATOR VOICE: gender and age impression; accent; timbre; pitch variation; estimated words per minute; energy and emotional changes (with timestamps); pauses (natural or uniform); audible breaths or room tone; any traits typical of synthetic speech. Give a judgement: human voice actor vs AI text-to-speech, with a confidence % and the evidence. If AI, which family it most resembles (ElevenLabs, Google Gemini TTS, OpenAI TTS, Microsoft Azure, cloned voice) and why. State that you cannot be certain.
4. CHARACTER VOICES / SKITS: are there spoken lines by characters or countries other than the narrator? For each: timestamp, the line, how the voice differs from the narrator (separate voice, pitch-shifted narrator, processed), and the comic timing (pause before/after). Say NONE if there are none.
5. MUSIC: genre, mood, tempo/energy, volume relative to the voice, every change, drop-out or sting with timestamps.
6. SOUND EFFECTS: list each with timestamp and type (whoosh, pop, impact, ding, ambience, etc.); total count and count per minute.
7. SILENCE AND PACING: any deliberate pauses or dead air; the longest stretch with no visual change; average seconds between visual changes.
8. CAPTIONS AND TEXT: caption style (font, colour, position, words per chunk, word highlighting); other on-screen text.
9. ENDING: last 5 seconds verbatim and what is on screen; does it loop back to the start; any call to action (spoken or on screen).
10. COUNTS: visual changes per minute; number of map zoom/pan moves; number of jokes or skit lines; number of distinct surprising facts (payoffs) and the timestamp of the first one.
11. RETENTION READ: in 4 bullets, the strongest and weakest moments for holding a viewer, with timestamps.
